claims.claim: ADM's global origination, crushing, refining and carbohydrate network links farm output and oilseeds/corn processing to food, feed and renewable-fuel demand; Q2 2026 evidence shows higher asset utilization and restored Barcarena operations converting infrastructure availability into higher throughput and profit.

Current causal strength is partly policy-mediated: finalized U.S. renewable-volume obligations, elevated energy prices and lower corn prices improved biofuel economics, so ADM's processing bottleneck control is valuable but not independent of policy and commodity regimes.

Targeted expansion at four North American crush facilities is intended to add about 700,000 metric tons of annual oilseed crush capacity, increasing ADM's ability to serve renewable-fuel and vegetable-oil demand while also creating additional feedstock demand for farmers.

causalEdges.mechanism: origination, storage, transport, crushing and wet milling aggregate dispersed crops into food/feed/fuel intermediates
processing capacity and restored/export infrastructure increase usable meal, vegetable oil, ethanol and ingredient supply
RVO obligations and energy/corn price relationships alter demand and blendstock economics

risks.risk: Successor bottleneck can migrate from processing capacity to feedstock availability, logistics, policy credits or end-market blend economics; additional crush capacity does not guarantee durable margin capture.
Substitution by alternative feedstocks, competing crush capacity or non-crop low-carbon fuels can weaken the renewable-fuel demand channel even while food/feed infrastructure remains useful.

contradictions.contradiction: Q2 network utilization and segment profit demonstrate operating leverage, but approximately $100M of favorable mark-to-market/timing effects and policy-supported biofuel economics mean headline profit cannot be treated as pure structural improvement.

unknowns.unknown: Durable incremental return on the announced 700,000-ton crush expansion across a normalized RVO/energy/feedstock environment is not yet observed.

claims.claim: The strongest current challenge to extrapolating ADM's Q2 earnings is composition rather than evidence of business failure: AS&O included about $100M of favorable mark-to-market/timing impacts and crushing/ethanol benefited from RVO policy and elevated energy prices.

Recent history provides a failure analog for margin normalization: Q4 2025 crushing operating profit fell 69% year over year despite higher global crush volumes because crush margins weakened, showing that throughput alone does not secure economics.

A prior material weakness in internal control over financial reporting related to segment-disclosure accounting is a governance/accounting risk that warrants continued verification, but it does not by itself invalidate current primary-source operating evidence.

risks.risk: Margin and earnings sensitivity to policy, commodity spreads, energy prices and mark-to-market timing can create confidence inflation if a favorable quarter is annualized without normalization.
Capacity additions can invite industry supply response; if crush capacity grows faster than renewable-oil/feed demand, utilization may rise while unit margins compress.
Prior segment-disclosure control weakness raises the value of independent filing-level reconciliation when Alpha constructs numeric score evidence.

contradictions.contradiction: Current strong crushing economics contrast with Q4 2025, when higher volumes coincided with a 69% operating-profit decline because margins weakened.
contradictions.disposition: resolved_as_scenario_sensitivity; retain as normalization constraint rather than present blocker

contradictions.contradiction: Headline Q2 profit growth is partly explained by timing effects and policy-sensitive economics rather than solely durable execution.
contradictions.disposition: resolved_as_earnings-quality adjustment; Alpha should normalize rather than reject evidence

unknowns.unknown: Whether internal-control remediation has fully eliminated the prior segment-disclosure weakness requires current filing-level confirmation beyond the evidence used here.
Long-run industry response to announced crush additions and competing low-carbon fuel pathways remains uncertain.
